Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (runtime-init-shutdown):
Map nodes n1-n18 and n81-n89. Read numbered files and return partial JSON mappings; note unsupported.

1	//! Surface represents a single terminal "surface". A terminal surface is
     2	//! a minimal "widget" where the terminal is drawn and responds to events
     3	//! such as keyboard and mouse. Each surface also creates and owns its pty
     4	//! session.
     5	//!
     6	//! The word "surface" is used because it is left to the higher level
     7	//! application runtime to determine if the surface is a window, a tab,
     8	//! a split, a preview pane in a larger window, etc. This struct doesn't care:
     9	//! it just draws and responds to events. The events come from the application
    10	//! runtime so the runtime can determine when and how those are delivered
    11	//! (i.e. with focus, without focus, and so on).
    12	const Surface = @This();
    13	
    14	const apprt = @import("apprt.zig");
    15	pub const Mailbox = apprt.surface.Mailbox;
    16	pub const Message = apprt.surface.Message;
    17	
    18	const std = @import("std");
    19	const builtin = @import("builtin");
    20	const assert = @import("quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    21	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    22	const ArenaAllocator = std.heap.ArenaAllocator;
    23	const global = @import("global.zig");
    24	const oni = @import("oniguruma");
    25	const simd = @import("simd/main.zig");
    26	const crash = @import("crash/main.zig");
    27	const unicode = @import("unicode/main.zig");
    28	const rendererpkg = @import("renderer.zig");

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();
   859	
   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864	
   865	    // Clean up our keyboard state
   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);
   868	    self.keyboard.table_stack.deinit(self.alloc);
   869	
   870	    // Clean up our font grid
   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);
   872	
   873	    // Clean up our render state
   874	    if (self.renderer_state.preedit) |p| self.alloc.free(p.codepoints);
   875	    self.alloc.destroy(self.renderer_state.mutex);
   876	    self.config.deinit();
   877	
   878	    log.info("surface closed id={x}", .{self.id});
   879	}

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();
   859	
   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864	
   865	    // Clean up our keyboard state
   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);
   868	    self.keyboard.table_stack.deinit(self.alloc);
   869	
   870	    // Clean up our font grid
   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);
   872	
   873	    // Clean up our render state
   874	    if (self.renderer_state.preedit) |p| self.alloc.free(p.codepoints);
   875	    self.alloc.destroy(self.renderer_state.mutex);
   876	    self.config.deinit();
   877	
   878	    log.info("surface closed id={x}", .{self.id});
   879	}

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();
   859	
   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864	
   865	    // Clean up our keyboard state
   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);
   868	    self.keyboard.table_stack.deinit(self.alloc);
   869	
   870	    // Clean up our font grid
   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);
   872	
   873	    // Clean up our render state
   874	    if (self.renderer_state.preedit) |p| self.alloc.free(p.codepoints);
   875	    self.alloc.destroy(self.renderer_state.mutex);
   876	    self.config.deinit();
   877	
   878	    log.info("surface closed id={x}", .{self.id});
   879	}

   150	/// how certain configurations take effect such as light/dark mode.
   151	/// This is managed completely by Ghostty core but an apprt action

   153	config_conditional_state: configpkg.ConditionalState,

   160	/// If we're not initially focused then apprts can call focusCallback

   166	visible: bool = true,

   190	/// The effect of an input event. This can be used by callers to take
   470	        };

   474	/// Create a new surface. This must be called from the main thread. The
   475	/// pointer to the memory for the surface must be provided and must be
   476	/// stable due to interfacing with various callbacks.
   477	pub fn init(
   478	    self: *Surface,
   479	    alloc: Allocator,
   480	    config_original: *const configpkg.Config,
   481	    app: *App,
   482	    rt_app: *apprt.runtime.App,
   483	    rt_surface: *apprt.runtime.Surface,
   484	) !void {
   485	    // Apply our conditional state. If we fail to apply the conditional state
   486	    // then we log and attempt to move forward with the old config.
   487	    var config_: ?configpkg.Config = config_original.changeConditionalState(
   488	        app.config_conditional_state,
   489	    ) catch |err| err: {
   490	        log.warn("failed to apply conditional state to config err={}", .{err});
   491	        break :err null;
   492	    };
   493	    defer if (config_) |*c| c.deinit();
   494	
   495	    // We want a config pointer for everything so we get that either
   496	    // based on our conditional state or the original config.
   497	    const config: *const configpkg.Config = if (config_) |*c| config: {
   498	        // We want to preserve our original working directory. We
   499	        // don't need to dupe memory here because termio will derive
   500	        // it. We preserve this so directory inheritance works.
   501	        c.@"working-directory" = config_original.@"working-directory";
   502	        break :config c;
   503	    } else config_original;
   504	
   505	    // Get our configuration
   506	    var derived_config = try DerivedConfig.init(alloc, config);
   507	    errdefer derived_config.deinit();
   508	
   509	    // Determine our DPI configurations so we can properly configure
   510	    // font points to pixels and handle other high-DPI scaling factors.
   511	    const content_scale = try rt_surface.getContentScale();
   512	    const x_dpi = content_scale.x * font.face.default_dpi;
   513	    const y_dpi = content_scale.y * font.face.default_dpi;
   514	    log.debug("xscale={} yscale={} xdpi={} ydpi={}", .{
   515	        content_scale.x,
   516	        content_scale.y,
   517	        x_dpi,
   518	        y_dpi,
   519	    });
   520	
   521	    // The font size we desire along with the DPI determined for the surface
   522	    const font_size: font.face.DesiredSize = .{
   523	        .points = config.@"font-size",
   524	        .xdpi = @intFromFloat(@round(x_dpi)),
   525	        .ydpi = @intFromFloat(@round(y_dpi)),
   526	    };
   527	
   528	    // Setup our font group. This will reuse an existing font group if
   529	    // it was already loaded.
   530	    const font_grid_key, const font_grid = try app.font_grid_set.ref(
   531	        &derived_config.font,
   532	        font_size,
   533	    );
   534	    errdefer app.font_grid_set.deref(font_grid_key);
   535	
   536	    // Build our size struct which has all the sizes we need.
   537	    const size: rendererpkg.Size = size: {
   538	        var size: rendererpkg.Size = .{
   539	            .screen = screen: {
   540	                const surface_size = try rt_surface.getSize();
   541	                break :screen .{
   542	                    .width = surface_size.width,
   543	                    .height = surface_size.height,
   544	                };
   545	            },
   546	
   547	            .cell = font_grid.cellSize(),
   548	            .padding = .{},
   549	        };
   550	
   551	        const explicit: rendererpkg.Padding = derived_config.scaledPadding(
   552	            x_dpi,
   553	            y_dpi,
   554	        );
   555	        if (derived_config.window_padding_balance != .false) {
   556	            size.balancePadding(explicit, derived_config.window_padding_balance);
   557	        } else {
   558	            size.padding = explicit;
   559	        }
   560	
   561	        break :size size;
   562	    };
   563	
   564	    // Initialize the render device if it hasn't been initialized already
   565	    const render_device = app.device orelse device: {
   566	        const device_options = try rt_surface.renderDeviceOptions();
   567	        const device: *rendererpkg.Device = try .init(alloc, device_options);
   568	        app.device = device;
   569	        break :device device;
   570	    };
   571	
   572	    // Create our terminal grid with the initial size
   573	    const app_mailbox: App.Mailbox = .{ .rt_app = rt_app, .mailbox = &app.mailbox };
   574	    var renderer_impl = renderer: {
   575	        // Renderer.init takes ownership of the config only on success, after
   576	        // which the errdefer below frees it, so this errdefer must end here.
   577	        var renderer_config = try Renderer.DerivedConfig.init(alloc, config);
   578	        errdefer renderer_config.deinit();
   579	
   580	        break :renderer try Renderer.init(alloc, .{
   581	            .device = render_device,
   582	            .config = renderer_config,
   583	            .font_grid = font_grid,
   584	            .size = size,
   585	            .surface_mailbox = .{ .surface = self, .app = app_mailbox },
   586	            .rt_surface = rt_surface,
   587	            .thread = &self.renderer_thread,
   588	        });
   589	    };
   590	    errdefer renderer_impl.deinit();
   591	
   592	    // The mutex used to protect our renderer state.
   593	    const mutex = try alloc.create(std.Io.Mutex);
   594	    mutex.* = .init;
   595	    errdefer alloc.destroy(mutex);
   596	
   597	    // Create the renderer thread
   598	    var render_thread = try rendererpkg.Thread.init(
   599	        alloc,
   600	        config,
   601	        rt_surface,
   602	        &self.renderer,
   603	        &self.renderer_state,
   604	    );
   605	    errdefer render_thread.deinit();
   606	
   607	    // Create the IO thread
   608	    var io_thread = try termio.Thread.init(alloc);
   609	    errdefer io_thread.deinit();
   610	
   611	    self.* = .{
   612	        .id = id: {
   613	            while (true) {
   614	                const candidate = candidate: {
   615	                    const rng_impl: std.Random.IoSource = .{ .io = global.io() };
   616	                    const rng = rng_impl.interface();
   617	                    break :candidate rng.int(u64);
   618	                };
   619	                if (candidate == 0) continue;
   620	                break :id candidate;
   621	            }
   622	        },
   623	        .alloc = alloc,
   624	        .app = app,
   625	        .rt_app = rt_app,
   626	        .rt_surface = rt_surface,
   627	        .font_grid_key = font_grid_key,
   628	        .font_size = font_size,
   629	        .font_size_adjusted = false,
   630	        .font_metrics = font_grid.metrics,
   631	        .renderer = renderer_impl,
   632	        .renderer_thread = render_thread,
   633	        .renderer_state = .{
   634	            .mutex = mutex,
   635	            .terminal = &self.io.terminal,
   636	        },
   637	        .renderer_thr = undefined,
   638	        .mouse = .{},
   639	        .keyboard = .{},
   640	        .io = undefined,
   641	        .io_thread = io_thread,
   642	        .io_thr = undefined,
   643	        .size = size,
   644	        .config = derived_config,
   645	
   646	        // Our conditional state is initialized to the app state. This
   647	        // lets us get the most likely correct color theme and so on.
   648	        .config_conditional_state = app.config_conditional_state,
   649	    };
   650	
   651	    // The command we're going to execute
   652	    const command: ?configpkg.Command = command: {
   653	        if (app.first) {
   654	            if (config.@"initial-command") |command| {
   655	                break :command command;
   656	            }
   657	        }
   658	        break :command config.command;
   659	    };
   660	
   700	        });
   701	        errdefer io_exec.deinit();
   702	
   703	        // Initialize our IO mailbox
   704	        var io_mailbox = try termio.Mailbox.initSPSC(alloc);
   705	        errdefer io_mailbox.deinit(alloc);
   706	
   707	        // Termio.init takes ownership of the config only on success.
   708	        var io_config = try termio.Termio.DerivedConfig.init(alloc, config);
   709	        errdefer io_config.deinit();
   710	
   711	        try termio.Termio.init(&self.io, alloc, .{
   712	            .size = size,
   713	            .full_config = config,
   714	            .config = io_config,
   715	            .backend = .{ .exec = io_exec },
   716	            .mailbox = io_mailbox,
   717	            .renderer_state = &self.renderer_state,
   718	            .renderer_wakeup = render_thread.wakeup,
   719	            .renderer_mailbox = render_thread.mailbox,
   720	            .surface_mailbox = .{ .surface = self, .app = app_mailbox },
   721	        });
   722	    }
   723	    // Outside the block, IO has now taken ownership of our temporary state
   724	    // so we can just defer this and not the subcomponents.
   725	    errdefer self.io.deinit();
   726	
   727	    // Report initial cell size on surface creation
   728	    _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   729	        .{ .surface = self },
   730	        .cell_size,
   731	        .{ .width = size.cell.width, .height = size.cell.height },
   732	    );
   733	
   734	    _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   735	        .{ .surface = self },
   736	        .size_limit,
   737	        .{
   738	            .min_width = size.cell.width * min_window_width_cells,
   739	            .min_height = size.cell.height * min_window_height_cells,
   740	            // No max:
   741	            .max_width = 0,
   742	            .max_height = 0,
   743	        },
   744	    );
   745	
   746	    // Call our size callback which handles all our retina setup
   747	    // Note: this shouldn't be necessary and when we clean up the surface
   748	    // init stuff we should get rid of this. But this is required because
   749	    // sizeCallback does retina-aware stuff we don't do here and don't want
   750	    // to duplicate.
   751	    try self.resize(self.size.screen);
   752	
   753	    // Start our renderer thread
   754	    self.renderer_thr = try std.Thread.spawn(
   755	        .{},
   756	        rendererpkg.Thread.threadMain,
   757	        .{&self.renderer_thread},
   758	    );
   759	    self.renderer_thr.setName(global.io(), "renderer") catch {};
   760	
   761	    // Start our IO thread
   762	    self.io_thr = try std.Thread.spawn(
   763	        .{},
   764	        termio.Thread.threadMain,
   765	        .{ &self.io_thread, &self.io },
   766	    );
   767	    self.io_thr.setName(global.io(), "io") catch {};
   768	
   769	    // Determine our initial window size if configured. We need to do this
   770	    // quite late in the process because our height/width are in grid dimensions,
   771	    // so we need to know our cell sizes first.
   772	    //
   773	    // Note: it is important to do this after the renderer is setup above.
   774	    // This allows the apprt to fully initialize the surface before we
   775	    // start messing with the window.
   776	    self.recomputeInitialSize() catch |err| {
   777	        // We don't treat this as a fatal error because not setting
   778	        // an initial size shouldn't stop our terminal from working.
   779	        log.warn("unable to set initial window size: {}", .{err});
   780	    };
   781	
   782	    if (config.title) |title| {
   783	        _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   784	            .{ .surface = self },
   785	            .set_title,
   786	            .{ .title = title },
   787	        );
   788	    } else if ((comptime builtin.target.os.tag == .linux) and
   789	        config.@"_xdg-terminal-exec")
   790	    xdg: {
   791	        // For xdg-terminal-exec execution we special-case and set the window
   792	        // title to the command being executed. This allows window managers
   793	        // to set custom styling based on the command being executed.
   794	        const v = command orelse break :xdg;
   795	        const title = v.string(alloc) catch |err| {
   796	            log.warn(
   797	                "error copying command for title, title will not be set err={}",
   798	                .{err},
   799	            );
   800	            break :xdg;
   801	        };
   802	        defer alloc.free(title);
   803	        _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   804	            .{ .surface = self },
   805	            .set_title,
   806	            .{ .title = title },
   807	        );
   808	    } else if (command) |cmd| switch (cmd) {
   809	        // If a user specifies a command it is appropriate to set the title as argv[0]
   810	        // we know in the case of a direct command it has been supplied by the user
   811	        .direct => |cmd_str| if (cmd_str.len != 0) {
   812	            _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   813	                .{ .surface = self },
   814	                .set_title,
   815	                .{ .title = cmd_str[0] },
   816	            );
   817	        },
   818	
   819	        // We won't set the title in the case the shell expands the command
   820	        // as that should typically be used to launch a shell which should
   821	        // set its own titles
   822	        .shell => {},
   823	    };
   824	
   825	    // We are no longer the first surface
   826	    app.first = false;
   827	}

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();
   859	
   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864	
   865	    // Clean up our keyboard state
   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);
   868	    self.keyboard.table_stack.deinit(self.alloc);
   869	
   870	    // Clean up our font grid
   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);
   872	
   873	    // Clean up our render state
   874	    if (self.renderer_state.preedit) |p| self.alloc.free(p.codepoints);
   875	    self.alloc.destroy(self.renderer_state.mutex);
   876	    self.config.deinit();
   877	
   878	    log.info("surface closed id={x}", .{self.id});
   879	}
   880	
   881	/// Close this surface. This will trigger the runtime to start the
   882	/// close process, which should ultimately deinitialize this surface.
   883	pub fn close(self: *Surface) void {
   884	    self.rt_surface.close(self.needsConfirmQuit());
   885	}

   887	/// Returns a mailbox that can be used to send messages to this surface.
   888	inline fn surfaceMailbox(self: *Surface) Mailbox {
   889	    return .{

   891	        .app = .{ .rt_app = self.rt_app, .mailbox = &self.app.mailbox },
   892	    };
   893	}

   896	///
   897	/// We centralize all our logic into this spot so we can intercept
   898	/// messages for example in readonly mode.
   899	fn queueIo(
   900	    self: *Surface,
   901	    msg: termio.Message,
   902	    mutex: termio.Termio.MutexState,
   903	) void {

   908	            .write_stable,

   914	
   915	            else => {},
   916	        }
   917	    }
   918	
   919	    self.io.queueMessage(msg, mutex);
   920	}

   925	pub fn draw(self: *Surface) !void {

   927	    // the main thread, so that they can update contents during resize.
   928	    try self.renderer.drawFrame(true);

1	//! Surface represents a single terminal "surface". A terminal surface is
     2	//! a minimal "widget" where the terminal is drawn and responds to events
     3	//! such as keyboard and mouse. Each surface also creates and owns its pty
     4	//! session.
     5	//!
     6	//! The word "surface" is used because it is left to the higher level
     7	//! application runtime to determine if the surface is a window, a tab,
     8	//! a split, a preview pane in a larger window, etc. This struct doesn't care:
     9	//! it just draws and responds to events. The events come from the application
    10	//! runtime so the runtime can determine when and how those are delivered
    11	//! (i.e. with focus, without focus, and so on).
    12	const Surface = @This();
    13	
    14	const apprt = @import("apprt.zig");
    15	pub const Mailbox = apprt.surface.Mailbox;
    16	pub const Message = apprt.surface.Message;
    17	
    18	const std = @import("std");
    19	const builtin = @import("builtin");
    20	const assert = @import("quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    21	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    22	const ArenaAllocator = std.heap.ArenaAllocator;
    23	const global = @import("global.zig");
    24	const oni = @import("oniguruma");
    25	const simd = @import("simd/main.zig");
    26	const crash = @import("crash/main.zig");
    27	const unicode = @import("unicode/main.zig");
    28	const rendererpkg = @import("renderer.zig");
    29	const termio = @import("termio.zig");
    30	const font = @import("font/main.zig");
    31	const Command = @import("Command.zig");
    32	const terminal = @import("terminal/main.zig");
    33	const configpkg = @import("config.zig");
    34	const Duration = configpkg.Config.Duration;
    35	const input = @import("input.zig");
    36	const App = @import("App.zig");
    37	const internal_os = @import("os/main.zig");
    38	const inspectorpkg = @import("inspector/main.zig");
    39	const SurfaceMouse = @import("surface_mouse.zig");
    40	const ProcessInfo = @import("pty.zig").ProcessInfo;
    41	
    42	const log = std.log.scoped(.surface);
    43	
    44	// The renderer implementation to use.
    45	const Renderer = rendererpkg.Renderer;

   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});

   848	    // shared values between the two threads.

   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();

1	//! This is the render state that is given to a renderer.
     2	
     3	const State = @This();
     4	
     5	const std = @import("std");
     6	const assert = std.debug.assert;
     7	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
     8	const Inspector = @import("../inspector/main.zig").Inspector;
     9	const terminalpkg = @import("../terminal/main.zig");
    10	const inputpkg = @import("../input.zig");
    11	const renderer = @import("../renderer.zig");
    12	
    13	/// The mutex that must be held while reading any of the data in the
    14	/// members of this state. Note that the state itself is NOT protected
    15	/// by the mutex and is NOT thread-safe, only the members values of the
    16	/// state (i.e. the terminal, devmode, etc. values).
    17	mutex: *std.Io.Mutex,
    18	
    19	/// The terminal data.
    20	terminal: *terminalpkg.Terminal,
    21	
    22	/// The terminal inspector, if any. This will be null while the inspector
    23	/// is not active and will be set when it is active.
    24	inspector: ?*Inspector = null,
    25	
    26	/// Dead key state. This will render the current dead key preedit text
    27	/// over the cursor. This currently only ever renders a single codepoint.
    28	/// Preedit can in theory be multiple codepoints long but that is left as
    29	/// a future exercise.
    30	preedit: ?Preedit = null,
    31	
    32	/// Mouse state. This only contains state relevant to what renderers
    33	/// need about the mouse.
    34	mouse: Mouse = .{},
    35	
    36	/// The number of threads currently waiting to acquire `mutex` via
    37	/// `lockDemand`. This is not protected by the mutex; it is read by
    38	/// hot lock/unlock loops (the IO parse thread) in `yieldToDemand` to
    39	/// decide whether to hand the mutex off before relocking it.
    40	demand: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    41	
    42	/// Handoff generation counter. Incremented (with a futex wake) by
    43	/// `unlockDemand` after a demanding waiter releases the mutex, so that
    44	/// `yieldToDemand` knows the waiter had its turn.
    45	handoff_gen: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    46	
    47	/// How long `yieldToDemand` sleeps waiting for a demanding waiter to
    48	/// take its turn before giving up. This bounds how long the IO parse
    49	/// thread can stall if a wake is lost or the waiter is descheduled; a
    50	/// demanding critical section (the renderer's frame snapshot) is
    51	/// microseconds, so one millisecond is generous.
    52	const handoff_timeout_ns = 1 * std.time.ns_per_ms;
    53	
    54	/// Acquire `mutex` while signaling demand for it. Use this instead of
    55	/// locking the mutex directly on threads that must not be starved by
    56	/// a hot lock/unlock loop (the renderer's frame snapshot). Must be
    57	/// released with `unlockDemand`; releasing with `mutex.unlock` keeps
    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out
    59	/// their full timeout.
    60	///
    61	/// Both `std.Thread.Mutex` and os_unfair_lock are unfair: a running
    62	/// thread that unlocks and immediately relocks beats a sleeping
    63	/// waiter every time, because the waiter must first be woken and
    64	/// scheduled. Under sustained pty output the IO parse thread is
    65	/// exactly such a loop, so without this signal the renderer can
    66	/// starve for as long as the output lasts.
    67	pub fn lockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    68	    _ = self.demand.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    69	    self.mutex.lockUncancelable(io);
    70	    const prev = self.demand.fetchSub(1, .monotonic);
    71	    assert(prev > 0);
    72	}
    73	
    74	/// Release `mutex` acquired via `lockDemand` and notify hot loops
    75	/// parked in `yieldToDemand` that the demanding waiter had its turn.
    76	pub fn unlockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    77	    self.mutex.unlock(io);
    78	    _ = self.handoff_gen.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    79	    io.futexWake(u32, &self.handoff_gen.raw, 1);
    80	}
    81	
    82	/// Called by hot lock/unlock loops between critical sections, with
    83	/// `mutex` NOT held: if a `lockDemand` waiter exists, sleep until it
    84	/// has acquired and released the mutex (or the timeout passes). This
    85	/// is the handoff that unfair mutexes never do on their own.
    86	///
    87	/// The orderings here are all monotonic because these atomics are a
    88	/// scheduling heuristic, not a synchronization boundary: the mutex
    89	/// itself orders the protected data, and the timeout bounds any
    90	/// staleness.
    91	pub fn yieldToDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    92	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    93	
    94	    // Snapshot the generation before rechecking demand: if the waiter
    95	    // acquires and releases between our check and the wait below, the
    96	    // generation no longer matches and timedWait returns immediately.
    97	    const gen = self.handoff_gen.load(.monotonic);
    98	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    99	    io.futexWaitTimeout(
   100	        u32,
   101	        &self.handoff_gen.raw,
   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },
   104	    ) catch {};
   105	}
   106	
   107	pub const Mouse = struct {
   108	    /// The point on the viewport where the mouse currently is. We use
   109	    /// viewport points to avoid the complexity of mapping the mouse to
   110	    /// the renderer state.
   111	    point: ?terminalpkg.point.Coordinate = null,
   112	
   113	    /// The mods that are currently active for the last mouse event.
   114	    /// This could really just be mods in general and we probably will
   115	    /// move it out of mouse state at some point.
   116	    mods: inputpkg.Mods = .{},

    47	/// How long `yieldToDemand` sleeps waiting for a demanding waiter to

    54	/// Acquire `mutex` while signaling demand for it. Use this instead of
    55	/// locking the mutex directly on threads that must not be starved by

    57	/// released with `unlockDemand`; releasing with `mutex.unlock` keeps
    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out

    65	/// exactly such a loop, so without this signal the renderer can
    66	/// starve for as long as the output lasts.

    68	    _ = self.demand.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);

   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },

    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out
    59	/// their full timeout.

    89	/// itself orders the protected data, and the timeout bounds any
    90	/// staleness.
    91	pub fn yieldToDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    92	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    93	
    94	    // Snapshot the generation before rechecking demand: if the waiter
    95	    // acquires and releases between our check and the wait below, the
    96	    // generation no longer matches and timedWait returns immediately.
    97	    const gen = self.handoff_gen.load(.monotonic);
    98	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;

   100	        u32,
   101	        &self.handoff_gen.raw,
   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },
   104	    ) catch {};

    54	/// Acquire `mutex` while signaling demand for it. Use this instead of
    55	/// locking the mutex directly on threads that must not be starved by
    56	/// a hot lock/unlock loop (the renderer's frame snapshot). Must be
    57	/// released with `unlockDemand`; releasing with `mutex.unlock` keeps
    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out
    59	/// their full timeout.

    61	/// Both `std.Thread.Mutex` and os_unfair_lock are unfair: a running
    62	/// thread that unlocks and immediately relocks beats a sleeping
    63	/// waiter every time, because the waiter must first be woken and
    64	/// scheduled. Under sustained pty output the IO parse thread is
    65	/// exactly such a loop, so without this signal the renderer can
    66	/// starve for as long as the output lasts.

    71	    assert(prev > 0);

    74	/// Release `mutex` acquired via `lockDemand` and notify hot loops
    75	/// parked in `yieldToDemand` that the demanding waiter had its turn.
    76	pub fn unlockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    77	    self.mutex.unlock(io);

    87	/// The orderings here are all monotonic because these atomics are a
    88	/// scheduling heuristic, not a synchronization boundary: the mutex
    89	/// itself orders the protected data, and the timeout bounds any
    90	/// staleness.
    91	pub fn yieldToDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    92	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    93	
    94	    // Snapshot the generation before rechecking demand: if the waiter
    95	    // acquires and releases between our check and the wait below, the
    96	    // generation no longer matches and timedWait returns immediately.
    97	    const gen = self.handoff_gen.load(.monotonic);
    98	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    99	    io.futexWaitTimeout(
   100	        u32,
   101	        &self.handoff_gen.raw,
   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },
   104	    ) catch {};

    37	/// `lockDemand`. This is not protected by the mutex; it is read by
    38	/// hot lock/unlock loops (the IO parse thread) in `yieldToDemand` to
    39	/// decide whether to hand the mutex off before relocking it.

    41	
    42	/// Handoff generation counter. Incremented (with a futex wake) by
    43	/// `unlockDemand` after a demanding waiter releases the mutex, so that
    44	/// `yieldToDemand` knows the waiter had its turn.
    45	handoff_gen: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    46	
    47	/// How long `yieldToDemand` sleeps waiting for a demanding waiter to
    48	/// take its turn before giving up. This bounds how long the IO parse
    49	/// thread can stall if a wake is lost or the waiter is descheduled; a
    50	/// demanding critical section (the renderer's frame snapshot) is
    51	/// microseconds, so one millisecond is generous.

    53	
    54	/// Acquire `mutex` while signaling demand for it. Use this instead of
    55	/// locking the mutex directly on threads that must not be starved by
    56	/// a hot lock/unlock loop (the renderer's frame snapshot). Must be
    57	/// released with `unlockDemand`; releasing with `mutex.unlock` keeps
    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out
    59	/// their full timeout.

    61	/// Both `std.Thread.Mutex` and os_unfair_lock are unfair: a running
    62	/// thread that unlocks and immediately relocks beats a sleeping
    63	/// waiter every time, because the waiter must first be woken and
    64	/// scheduled. Under sustained pty output the IO parse thread is
    65	/// exactly such a loop, so without this signal the renderer can
    66	/// starve for as long as the output lasts.

    68	    _ = self.demand.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    69	    self.mutex.lockUncancelable(io);

    75	/// parked in `yieldToDemand` that the demanding waiter had its turn.
    76	pub fn unlockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    77	    self.mutex.unlock(io);
    78	    _ = self.handoff_gen.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);

    83	/// `mutex` NOT held: if a `lockDemand` waiter exists, sleep until it

    88	/// scheduling heuristic, not a synchronization boundary: the mutex

    90	/// staleness.
    91	pub fn yieldToDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    92	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;

   101	        &self.handoff_gen.raw,
   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },

1	//! Surface represents a single terminal "surface". A terminal surface is
     2	//! a minimal "widget" where the terminal is drawn and responds to events
     3	//! such as keyboard and mouse. Each surface also creates and owns its pty
     4	//! session.
     5	//!
     6	//! The word "surface" is used because it is left to the higher level
     7	//! application runtime to determine if the surface is a window, a tab,
     8	//! a split, a preview pane in a larger window, etc. This struct doesn't care:
     9	//! it just draws and responds to events. The events come from the application
    10	//! runtime so the runtime can determine when and how those are delivered
    11	//! (i.e. with focus, without focus, and so on).
    12	const Surface = @This();
    13	
    14	const apprt = @import("apprt.zig");
    15	pub const Mailbox = apprt.surface.Mailbox;
    16	pub const Message = apprt.surface.Message;
    17	
    18	const std = @import("std");
    19	const builtin = @import("builtin");
    20	const assert = @import("quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    21	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    22	const ArenaAllocator = std.heap.ArenaAllocator;
    23	const global = @import("global.zig");
    24	const oni = @import("oniguruma");
    25	const simd = @import("simd/main.zig");
    26	const crash = @import("crash/main.zig");
    27	const unicode = @import("unicode/main.zig");
    28	const rendererpkg = @import("renderer.zig");
    29	const termio = @import("termio.zig");
    30	const font = @import("font/main.zig");
    31	const Command = @import("Command.zig");
    32	const terminal = @import("terminal/main.zig");
    33	const configpkg = @import("config.zig");
    34	const Duration = configpkg.Config.Duration;
    35	const input = @import("input.zig");
    36	const App = @import("App.zig");
    37	const internal_os = @import("os/main.zig");
    38	const inspectorpkg = @import("inspector/main.zig");
    39	const SurfaceMouse = @import("surface_mouse.zig");
    40	const ProcessInfo = @import("pty.zig").ProcessInfo;
    41	
    42	const log = std.log.scoped(.surface);
    43	
    44	// The renderer implementation to use.
    45	const Renderer = rendererpkg.Renderer;
    46	
    47	/// Minimum window size in cells. This is used to prevent the window from
    48	/// being resized to a size that is too small to be useful. These defaults
    49	/// are chosen to match the default size of Mac's Terminal.app, but is
    50	/// otherwise somewhat arbitrary.
    51	pub const min_window_width_cells: u32 = 10;
    52	pub const min_window_height_cells: u32 = 4;
    53	
    54	/// Minimum size in cells that the running program can resize the window
    55	/// to (CSI 8 t). This is larger than the minimum window size so that a
    56	/// program can't shrink the window to hide its output.
    57	const min_resize_width_cells: u32 = 40;
    58	const min_resize_height_cells: u32 = 10;
    59	
    60	/// The maximum number of key tables that can be active at any
    61	/// given time. `activate_key_table` calls after this are ignored.
    62	const max_active_key_tables = 8;
    63	
    64	/// Unique ID used to identify this surface for IPC purposes. It is
    65	/// exposed to the commands running in surfaces as the environment variable
    66	/// GHOSTTY_SURFACE_ID. It must not be zero as zero is used to incicate a null
    67	/// value when communicating an ID over DBus as DBus does not allow null/maybe
    68	/// values.
    69	id: u64,
    70	
    71	/// Allocator
    72	alloc: Allocator,
    73	
    74	/// The app that this surface is attached to.
    75	app: *App,
    76	
    77	/// The windowing system surface and app.
    78	rt_app: *apprt.runtime.App,
    79	rt_surface: *apprt.runtime.Surface,
    80	
    81	/// The font structures
    82	font_grid_key: font.SharedGridSet.Key,
    83	font_size: font.face.DesiredSize,
    84	font_metrics: font.Metrics,
    85	
    86	/// This keeps track of if the font size was ever modified. If it wasn't,
    87	/// then config reloading will change the font. If it was manually adjusted,
    88	/// we don't change it on config reload since we assume the user wants
    89	/// a specific size.
    90	font_size_adjusted: bool,
    91	
    92	/// The renderer for this surface.
    93	renderer: Renderer,
    94	
    95	/// The render state
    96	renderer_state: rendererpkg.State,
    97	
    98	/// The renderer thread manager
    99	renderer_thread: rendererpkg.Thread,
   100	
   101	/// The actual thread
   102	renderer_thr: std.Thread,
   103	
   104	/// Mouse state.
   105	mouse: Mouse,
   106	
   107	/// Keyboard input state.
   108	keyboard: Keyboard,
   109	
   110	/// A currently pressed key. This is used so that we can send a keyboard
   111	/// release event when the surface is unfocused. Note that when the surface
   112	/// is refocused, a key press event may not be sent again -- this depends
   113	/// on the apprt (UI framework) in use, but we want to consistently send
   114	/// a release.
   115	///
   116	/// This is only sent when a keypress event results in a key event being
   117	/// sent to the pty. If it is consumed by a keybinding or other action,
   118	/// this is not set.
   119	///
   120	/// Also note the utf8 value is not valid for this event so some unfocused
   121	/// release events may not send exactly the right data within Kitty keyboard
   122	/// events. This seems unspecified in the spec so for now I'm okay with
   123	/// this. Plus, its only for release events where the key text is far
   124	/// less important.
   125	pressed_key: ?input.KeyEvent = null,
   126	
   127	/// The hash value of the last keybinding trigger that we performed. This
   128	/// is only set if the last key input matched a keybinding, consumed it,
   129	/// and performed it. This is used to prevent sending release/repeat events
   130	/// for handled bindings.
   131	last_binding_trigger: u64 = 0,
   132	
   133	/// The terminal IO handler.
   134	io: termio.Termio,
   135	io_thread: termio.Thread,
   136	io_thr: std.Thread,
   137	
   138	/// Terminal inspector
   139	inspector: ?*inspectorpkg.Inspector = null,
   140	
   141	/// All our sizing information.
   142	size: rendererpkg.Size,
   143	
   144	/// The configuration derived from the main config. We "derive" it so that
   145	/// we don't have a shared pointer hanging around that we need to worry about
   146	/// the lifetime of. This makes updating config at runtime easier.
   147	config: DerivedConfig,
   148	
   149	/// The conditional state of the configuration. This can affect
   150	/// how certain configurations take effect such as light/dark mode.
   151	/// This is managed completely by Ghostty core but an apprt action
   152	/// is sent whenever this changes.
   153	config_conditional_state: configpkg.ConditionalState,
   154	
   155	/// This is set to true if our IO thread notifies us our child exited.
   156	/// This is used to determine if we need to confirm, hold open, etc.
   157	child_exited: bool = false,
   158	
   159	/// We maintain our focus state and assume we're focused by default.
   160	/// If we're not initially focused then apprts can call focusCallback
   161	/// to let us know.
   162	focused: bool = true,
   163	
   164	/// Whether this surface may be visible. Unknown visibility is considered
   165	/// visible so reporting remains conservative.
   166	visible: bool = true,
   167	
   168	/// Used to determine whether to continuously scroll.
   169	selection_scroll_active: bool = false,
   170	
   171	/// True if the surface is in read-only mode. When read-only, no input
   172	/// is sent to the PTY but terminal-level operations like selections,
   173	/// (native) scrolling, and copy keybinds still work. Warn before quit is
   174	/// always enabled in this state.
   175	readonly: bool = false,
   176	
   177	/// Used to send notifications that long running commands have finished.
   178	/// Requires that shell integration be active. Should represent a nanosecond
   179	/// precision timestamp. It does not necessarily need to correspond to the
   180	/// actual time, but we must be able to compare two subsequent timestamps to get
   181	/// the wall clock time that has elapsed between timestamps.
   182	command_timer: ?std.Io.Timestamp = null,
   183	
   184	/// Search state
   185	search: ?Search = null,
   186	
   187	/// Used to rate limit BEL handling.
   188	last_bell_time: ?std.Io.Timestamp = null,
   189	
   190	/// The effect of an input event. This can be used by callers to take
   470	        };
   471	    }
   472	};
   473	
   474	/// Create a new surface. This must be called from the main thread. The
   475	/// pointer to the memory for the surface must be provided and must be
   476	/// stable due to interfacing with various callbacks.
   477	pub fn init(
   478	    self: *Surface,
   479	    alloc: Allocator,
   480	    config_original: *const configpkg.Config,
   481	    app: *App,
   482	    rt_app: *apprt.runtime.App,
   483	    rt_surface: *apprt.runtime.Surface,
   484	) !void {
   485	    // Apply our conditional state. If we fail to apply the conditional state
   486	    // then we log and attempt to move forward with the old config.
   487	    var config_: ?configpkg.Config = config_original.changeConditionalState(
   488	        app.config_conditional_state,
   489	    ) catch |err| err: {
   490	        log.warn("failed to apply conditional state to config err={}", .{err});
   491	        break :err null;
   492	    };
   493	    defer if (config_) |*c| c.deinit();
   494	
   495	    // We want a config pointer for everything so we get that either
   496	    // based on our conditional state or the original config.
   497	    const config: *const configpkg.Config = if (config_) |*c| config: {
   498	        // We want to preserve our original working directory. We
   499	        // don't need to dupe memory here because termio will derive
   500	        // it. We preserve this so directory inheritance works.
   501	        c.@"working-directory" = config_original.@"working-directory";
   502	        break :config c;
   503	    } else config_original;
   504	
   505	    // Get our configuration
   506	    var derived_config = try DerivedConfig.init(alloc, config);
   507	    errdefer derived_config.deinit();
   508	
   509	    // Determine our DPI configurations so we can properly configure
   510	    // font points to pixels and handle other high-DPI scaling factors.
   511	    const content_scale = try rt_surface.getContentScale();
   512	    const x_dpi = content_scale.x * font.face.default_dpi;
   513	    const y_dpi = content_scale.y * font.face.default_dpi;
   514	    log.debug("xscale={} yscale={} xdpi={} ydpi={}", .{
   515	        content_scale.x,
   516	        content_scale.y,
   517	        x_dpi,
   518	        y_dpi,
   519	    });
   520	
   521	    // The font size we desire along with the DPI determined for the surface
   522	    const font_size: font.face.DesiredSize = .{
   523	        .points = config.@"font-size",
   524	        .xdpi = @intFromFloat(@round(x_dpi)),
   525	        .ydpi = @intFromFloat(@round(y_dpi)),
   526	    };
   527	
   528	    // Setup our font group. This will reuse an existing font group if
   529	    // it was already loaded.
   530	    const font_grid_key, const font_grid = try app.font_grid_set.ref(
   531	        &derived_config.font,
   532	        font_size,
   533	    );
   534	    errdefer app.font_grid_set.deref(font_grid_key);
   535	
   536	    // Build our size struct which has all the sizes we need.
   537	    const size: rendererpkg.Size = size: {
   538	        var size: rendererpkg.Size = .{
   539	            .screen = screen: {
   540	                const surface_size = try rt_surface.getSize();
   541	                break :screen .{
   542	                    .width = surface_size.width,
   543	                    .height = surface_size.height,
   544	                };
   545	            },
   546	
   547	            .cell = font_grid.cellSize(),
   548	            .padding = .{},
   549	        };
   550	
   551	        const explicit: rendererpkg.Padding = derived_config.scaledPadding(
   552	            x_dpi,
   553	            y_dpi,
   554	        );

   556	            size.balancePadding(explicit, derived_config.window_padding_balance);
   557	        } else {
   558	            size.padding = explicit;
   559	        }
   560	
   561	        break :size size;
   562	    };
   563	
   564	    // Initialize the render device if it hasn't been initialized already
   565	    const render_device = app.device orelse device: {
   566	        const device_options = try rt_surface.renderDeviceOptions();
   567	        const device: *rendererpkg.Device = try .init(alloc, device_options);
   568	        app.device = device;
   569	        break :device device;
   570	    };
   571	
   572	    // Create our terminal grid with the initial size
   573	    const app_mailbox: App.Mailbox = .{ .rt_app = rt_app, .mailbox = &app.mailbox };
   574	    var renderer_impl = renderer: {
   575	        // Renderer.init takes ownership of the config only on success, after
   576	        // which the errdefer below frees it, so this errdefer must end here.
   577	        var renderer_config = try Renderer.DerivedConfig.init(alloc, config);
   578	        errdefer renderer_config.deinit();

   580	        break :renderer try Renderer.init(alloc, .{
   581	            .device = render_device,
   582	            .config = renderer_config,
   583	            .font_grid = font_grid,
   584	            .size = size,
   585	            .surface_mailbox = .{ .surface = self, .app = app_mailbox },
   586	            .rt_surface = rt_surface,
   587	            .thread = &self.renderer_thread,
   588	        });
   589	    };

   591	
   592	    // The mutex used to protect our renderer state.
   593	    const mutex = try alloc.create(std.Io.Mutex);
   594	    mutex.* = .init;
   595	    errdefer alloc.destroy(mutex);

   597	    // Create the renderer thread
   598	    var render_thread = try rendererpkg.Thread.init(
   599	        alloc,
   600	        config,
   601	        rt_surface,
   602	        &self.renderer,
   603	        &self.renderer_state,
   604	    );

   606	
   607	    // Create the IO thread
   608	    var io_thread = try termio.Thread.init(alloc);

   611	    self.* = .{
   612	        .id = id: {

   615	                    const rng_impl: std.Random.IoSource = .{ .io = global.io() };

   618	                };

   621	            }

   623	        .alloc = alloc,
   624	        .app = app,
   625	        .rt_app = rt_app,
   626	        .rt_surface = rt_surface,
   627	        .font_grid_key = font_grid_key,
   628	        .font_size = font_size,
   629	        .font_size_adjusted = false,
   630	        .font_metrics = font_grid.metrics,
   631	        .renderer = renderer_impl,
   632	        .renderer_thread = render_thread,

   635	            .terminal = &self.io.terminal,
   636	        },

   638	        .mouse = .{},
   639	        .keyboard = .{},
   640	        .io = undefined,
   641	        .io_thread = io_thread,
   642	        .io_thr = undefined,
   643	        .size = size,
   644	        .config = derived_config,
   645	
   646	        // Our conditional state is initialized to the app state. This

   648	        .config_conditional_state = app.config_conditional_state,

   656	            }

   658	        break :command config.command;

   700	        });

   702	
   703	        // Initialize our IO mailbox

   707	        // Termio.init takes ownership of the config only on success.

   713	            .full_config = config,
   714	            .config = io_config,
   715	            .backend = .{ .exec = io_exec },
   716	            .mailbox = io_mailbox,
   717	            .renderer_state = &self.renderer_state,
   718	            .renderer_wakeup = render_thread.wakeup,
   719	            .renderer_mailbox = render_thread.mailbox,
   720	            .surface_mailbox = .{ .surface = self, .app = app_mailbox },
   721	        });
   722	    }
   723	    // Outside the block, IO has now taken ownership of our temporary state
   724	    // so we can just defer this and not the subcomponents.
   725	    errdefer self.io.deinit();
   726	
   727	    // Report initial cell size on surface creation
   728	    _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   729	        .{ .surface = self },
   730	        .cell_size,
   731	        .{ .width = size.cell.width, .height = size.cell.height },
   732	    );
   733	
   734	    _ = try rt_app.performAction(
   735	        .{ .surface = self },
   736	        .size_limit,
   737	        .{
   738	            .min_width = size.cell.width * min_window_width_cells,
   739	            .min_height = size.cell.height * min_window_height_cells,
   740	            // No max:
   741	            .max_width = 0,
   742	            .max_height = 0,
   743	        },
   744	    );
   745	
   746	    // Call our size callback which handles all our retina setup
   747	    // Note: this shouldn't be necessary and when we clean up the surface
   748	    // init stuff we should get rid of this. But this is required because
   749	    // sizeCallback does retina-aware stuff we don't do here and don't want
   750	    // to duplicate.
   751	    try self.resize(self.size.screen);

   753	    // Start our renderer thread
   754	    self.renderer_thr = try std.Thread.spawn(
   755	        .{},
   756	        rendererpkg.Thread.threadMain,
   757	        .{&self.renderer_thread},
   758	    );

   760	
   761	    // Start our IO thread
   762	    self.io_thr = try std.Thread.spawn(
   763	        .{},
   764	        termio.Thread.threadMain,

   769	    // Determine our initial window size if configured. We need to do this
   770	    // quite late in the process because our height/width are in grid dimensions,
   771	    // so we need to know our cell sizes first.
   772	    //

   774	    // This allows the apprt to fully initialize the surface before we
   775	    // start messing with the window.
   776	    self.recomputeInitialSize() catch |err| {

   778	        // an initial size shouldn't stop our terminal from working.
   779	        log.warn("unable to set initial window size: {}", .{err});
   780	    };

   782	    if (config.title) |title| {
   783	        _ = try rt_app.performAction(

   785	            .set_title,
   786	            .{ .title = title },

   794	        const v = command orelse break :xdg;

   801	        };

   806	            .{ .title = title },

   819	        // We won't set the title in the case the shell expands the command

   822	        .shell => {},
   823	    };

   825	    // We are no longer the first surface
   826	    app.first = false;
   827	}

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();

   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {

   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();
   859	
   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {

   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);

1	//! This is the render state that is given to a renderer.
     2	
     3	const State = @This();
     4	
     5	const std = @import("std");
     6	const assert = std.debug.assert;
     7	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
     8	const Inspector = @import("../inspector/main.zig").Inspector;
     9	const terminalpkg = @import("../terminal/main.zig");
    10	const inputpkg = @import("../input.zig");
    11	const renderer = @import("../renderer.zig");
    12	
    13	/// The mutex that must be held while reading any of the data in the
    14	/// members of this state. Note that the state itself is NOT protected
    15	/// by the mutex and is NOT thread-safe, only the members values of the
    16	/// state (i.e. the terminal, devmode, etc. values).
    17	mutex: *std.Io.Mutex,
    18	
    19	/// The terminal data.
    20	terminal: *terminalpkg.Terminal,
    21	
    22	/// The terminal inspector, if any. This will be null while the inspector
    23	/// is not active and will be set when it is active.
    24	inspector: ?*Inspector = null,
    25	
    26	/// Dead key state. This will render the current dead key preedit text
    27	/// over the cursor. This currently only ever renders a single codepoint.
    28	/// Preedit can in theory be multiple codepoints long but that is left as
    29	/// a future exercise.
    30	preedit: ?Preedit = null,
    31	
    32	/// Mouse state. This only contains state relevant to what renderers
    33	/// need about the mouse.
    34	mouse: Mouse = .{},
    35	
    36	/// The number of threads currently waiting to acquire `mutex` via
    37	/// `lockDemand`. This is not protected by the mutex; it is read by
    38	/// hot lock/unlock loops (the IO parse thread) in `yieldToDemand` to
    39	/// decide whether to hand the mutex off before relocking it.
    40	demand: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    41	
    42	/// Handoff generation counter. Incremented (with a futex wake) by
    43	/// `unlockDemand` after a demanding waiter releases the mutex, so that
    44	/// `yieldToDemand` knows the waiter had its turn.
    45	handoff_gen: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    46	
    47	/// How long `yieldToDemand` sleeps waiting for a demanding waiter to
    48	/// take its turn before giving up. This bounds how long the IO parse
    49	/// thread can stall if a wake is lost or the waiter is descheduled; a
    50	/// demanding critical section (the renderer's frame snapshot) is
    51	/// microseconds, so one millisecond is generous.
    52	const handoff_timeout_ns = 1 * std.time.ns_per_ms;
    53	
    54	/// Acquire `mutex` while signaling demand for it. Use this instead of
    55	/// locking the mutex directly on threads that must not be starved by
    56	/// a hot lock/unlock loop (the renderer's frame snapshot). Must be
    57	/// released with `unlockDemand`; releasing with `mutex.unlock` keeps
    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out
    59	/// their full timeout.
    60	///
    61	/// Both `std.Thread.Mutex` and os_unfair_lock are unfair: a running
    62	/// thread that unlocks and immediately relocks beats a sleeping
    63	/// waiter every time, because the waiter must first be woken and
    64	/// scheduled. Under sustained pty output the IO parse thread is
    65	/// exactly such a loop, so without this signal the renderer can
    66	/// starve for as long as the output lasts.
    67	pub fn lockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    68	    _ = self.demand.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    69	    self.mutex.lockUncancelable(io);
    70	    const prev = self.demand.fetchSub(1, .monotonic);
    71	    assert(prev > 0);
    72	}
    73	
    74	/// Release `mutex` acquired via `lockDemand` and notify hot loops
    75	/// parked in `yieldToDemand` that the demanding waiter had its turn.
    76	pub fn unlockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    77	    self.mutex.unlock(io);
    78	    _ = self.handoff_gen.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    79	    io.futexWake(u32, &self.handoff_gen.raw, 1);
    80	}
    81	
    82	/// Called by hot lock/unlock loops between critical sections, with
    83	/// `mutex` NOT held: if a `lockDemand` waiter exists, sleep until it
    84	/// has acquired and released the mutex (or the timeout passes). This
    85	/// is the handoff that unfair mutexes never do on their own.
    86	///
    87	/// The orderings here are all monotonic because these atomics are a
    88	/// scheduling heuristic, not a synchronization boundary: the mutex
    89	/// itself orders the protected data, and the timeout bounds any
    90	/// staleness.
    91	pub fn yieldToDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    92	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    93	
    94	    // Snapshot the generation before rechecking demand: if the waiter
    95	    // acquires and releases between our check and the wait below, the
    96	    // generation no longer matches and timedWait returns immediately.
    97	    const gen = self.handoff_gen.load(.monotonic);
    98	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    99	    io.futexWaitTimeout(
   100	        u32,
   101	        &self.handoff_gen.raw,
   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },
   104	    ) catch {};
   105	}

   107	pub const Mouse = struct {
   108	    /// The point on the viewport where the mouse currently is. We use
   109	    /// viewport points to avoid the complexity of mapping the mouse to
   110	    /// the renderer state.

   141	        // Use an arena to simplify memory management below

   144	        const alloc = arena.allocator();

   147	        // the error message. It might be better in the future to send
   148	        // the error to the surface thread and let the apprt deal with it
   149	        // in some way but this works for now. Without this, the user would
   150	        // just see a blank terminal window.
   151	        io.renderer_state.mutex.lockUncancelable(global.io());
   152	        defer io.renderer_state.mutex.unlock(global.io());

   173	                    \\This error is usually due to having too many terminal
   174	                    \\windows open or having another program that is using too
   175	                    \\many pty devices.

  1308	    /// ahead of the parse stage before it blocks, which (via the
  1309	    /// kernel pty queue) is also what preserves flow control to the
  1310	    /// child. Empirically chosen through measurements on an M4 Max.
  1311	    /// Less than 4 there are minor slowdowns, above 4 there are no
  1312	    /// improvements.

  1314	
  1315	    /// The capacity of each gather buffer. One batch is also the unit

  1317	    /// this bounds both gather latency and lock hold time.
  1318	    const buffer_capacity = 64 * 1024;
  1319	
  1320	    /// How many gathered bytes mark a stream as saturated. The macOS
  1321	    /// kernel tty output queue hands the master at most about 1 KiB
  1322	    /// per read, so gathering a full 1 KiB means the writer filled
  1323	    /// the queue (a bulk stream worth briefly waiting on), while
  1324	    /// anything smaller is an interactive trickle that must be
  1325	    /// delivered with no added latency.
  1326	    const bridge_threshold = 1024;

  1332	    /// The writer refills the drained kernel queue within a few
  1333	    /// microseconds, while a sleep and wakeup through poll costs
  1334	    /// several more. If the gather stage sleeps on every refill gap,
  1335	    /// the whole pipeline degenerates to lockstep with the writer at
  1336	    /// about 1 KiB per wakeup. A short burst of nonblocking reads

  1338	    /// to 16 retries catches over 90% of the gaps and nearly doubles
